definition: without AI the person would not have contributed, or AI made it much easier to start (skill, time or effort)
inclusion: the person says they would not have had the skill, time or patience to contribute without AI, or that AI lowered the effort to start
exclusion: AI helped to understand the code or the workflow, without saying the contribution would not have happened (onboarding)
examples: "without AI I wouldn't be technically able to do any of these things" (N11) | "I wouldn't have the time otherwise." (N30) | "the bar for contribution is lower now, but the bar for trust is higher" (M31)

definition: AI helped to understand the code and the project workflow
inclusion: AI was used to navigate the repository, understand the codebase, its conventions or the contribution workflow
exclusion: AI only wrote or reviewed the code, with no mention of understanding the project (tool)
examples: "it helped me understand the project, its workflow, and the codebase more quickly" (N5) | "AI was used to navigate the repo, understand its culture and conventions" (N35) | "it just made the onboarding process easier" (N37)

definition: AI widens the community (users become developers)
inclusion: AI lets people who could not contribute before, such as users or beginners, join the developer community
exclusion: the effect is only on the respondent's own contribution (lowers_barrier)
examples: "using AI could enhance the community by expanding the community, by allowing the community of users to move into the community of developers" (N9) | "make open-source projects more accessible to beginners" (N38)

definition: AI as a collaborator or peer, not as a tool
inclusion: AI is described as a collaborator, peer or member of the team
exclusion: AI is described as a tool under human control (tool)
examples: "AI agents are equal collaborators no different from people" (N28)

definition: AI is just a tool; the human stays responsible
inclusion: AI is called a tool like any other, and the human keeps the responsibility for the contribution
exclusion: the answer makes the effect of AI depend on how it is used or reviewed (human_loop)
examples: "LLMs are just tools" (N10) | "AI is just a tool; what matters is quality and review, not who or what wrote the code" (N23) | "I think AI agents are just tools rather than things in our community" (M20)

definition: depends on how it is used / on the human reviewing it
inclusion: the effect of AI depends on how it is used, on a human reviewing and understanding the output, or on the autonomy given to the agent
exclusion: AI is called a neutral tool with no condition attached (tool)
examples: "If it still goes through the course of a maintainer or contributor, receives critique and is addressed properly then I believe it's healthy AI usage." (N16) | "When used properly with a Human in the loop, it's not any different from human-only PRs." (M16) | "when it's used by people who do not understand what they're doing and wouldn't be able to do it by themselves, it's usually a net negative" (M22)

category: AI as a threat to the community
inclusion: low-effort or low-value AI contributions, noise, volume that overloads review, or contributors seeking credit
exclusion: the concern is the loss of human contact or learning, not the quality or volume of contributions (interaction)
examples: "AI enables low effort submissions which introduces noise into the system." (N3) | "A lot of low value PRs and issues are being opened" (N39) | "AI enables people who seem to just want credit / name recognition." (M18)

category: AI as a threat to the community
definition: loss of interaction, learning or human contact
inclusion: AI reduces communication between people, the learning that comes from it, or the human connection in reviews
exclusion: the concern is the quality or volume of AI contributions (slop) or the respondent's ownership of their own work (detachment)
examples: "You can learn from it, but its a very different feeling than learning from other people working on the project." (N26) | "If the day is filled with only good AI PR reviews, it can be really draining and lonely." (M13) | "It removes the processes that cause contributors to develop expertise" (M46)

category: AI as a threat to the community
definition: AI weakens the sense of ownership of one's own work
inclusion: writing code with AI reduces the respondent's sense of ownership of their own contribution
exclusion: the loss concerns contact with other people (interaction)
examples: "With AI you have very little sense of ownership." (M42)

definition: mentions impostor syndrome or lack of confidence
inclusion: the respondent mentions impostor syndrome or a lack of confidence in their own ability, with or without AI
exclusion: AI only saved time or effort, with no mention of confidence (lowers_barrier)
examples: "I sometimes struggle with impostor syndrome" (N4) | "the assurance of correctness and validation from AI agent certainly removed the imposter syndrome" (N35)
